clue.text: Argument of staff with numbers of Romans

parts.note: a pole is a long staff or rod
M, I and C are Roman numerals: a thousand, one and a hundred

explanation.surface: A row breaks out between the staff and a bunch of Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a forceful written or spoken attack, a combative piece of disputation.

clue.text: Unexpected danger of underground disaster

parts.note: a pit is an underground mine or hole
a fall is a downfall, a ruin or disaster

explanation.surface: A sudden hazard of a disaster underground, like a mine collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden hazard or trap that catches people unawares.

clue.text: Left on old farm, looking well ahead

parts.note: taken as written
a grange is a farmhouse with its buildings, an old word for a farm

explanation.surface: Someone left on the old farm is looking well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking well' suggests good health, but with 'ahead' it means planning far into the future. A grange is a country house with farm buildings in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-range forecast or plan covers a period far into the future.

clue.text: Place for rest of the drivers

definitions.text: Place for rest of the drivers

parts.words: Place for rest of the drivers
parts.note: 'rest of the drivers' reads as the remaining drivers, but it means a place where motorists stop to sleep

explanation.surface: A place for the remaining drivers to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside hotel built for motorists, with parking by the rooms.

clue.text: Special language one's associated with East

definitions.text: Special language one's associated with East

parts.note: cant is the jargon or special language of a particular group
one's gives ONES, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A special tongue is linked with the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a language associated with the East, spoken in southern China and Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese tongue is spoken in Guangdong and Hong Kong, a language of the Far East.

clue.text: Company concealing it with face-saving device

indicators.note: something concealing another holds it out of sight inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a visor shields the face, literally saving it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm hides its business behind a public-relations exercise to save face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face-saving device' suggests a PR trick, but it is the literal shield over a face. 'Company' is the definition: a guest is the company you have.
explanation.definitionFit: When you have company, someone has called on you: a guest who has come to call.

clue.text: Inoculated any odd part for this

definitions.text: Inoculated any odd part for this

parts.words: Inoculated any odd part for this
parts.note: take any odd-numbered letter of the word Inoculated, first, third, fifth and so on, and it is one of a, e, i, o, u

explanation.surface: Someone was inoculated in some odd part of the body for this.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of INOCULATED are I, O, U, A, E: every vowel, one each.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the odd-placed letters is a, e, i, o or u, the letters that are not consonants.

clue.text: Raised vessels, and put out from port

indicators.note: in a down clue a word raised is read from bottom to top, so it is turned round

parts.note: vats are large vessels for liquid
to put someone out is to annoy them, to anger them

explanation.surface: Ships were hoisted up and then put out to sea from harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns VATS into STAV. Stavanger is a port city in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Stavanger is a seaport on Norway's south-west coast, centre of its oil industry.

clue.text: The shortest form of thank-you letter

parts.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thanks, about as short as it gets

explanation.surface: The briefest possible thank-you note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests a written note, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Changing sides, in a race admitted by the bookies

indicators.note: something admitted by another is let inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the ring is the betting area at a racecourse where bookmakers stand
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: In a race, a jockey switches allegiance, as the bookmakers concede.
explanation.walkthrough: To rat is to desert your party or side, so ratting is defecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to betray or desert one's side, especially in politics.

clue.text: Dogma — point found in early work of St Paul

indicators.note: a point found in something sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: before his missionary career Paul of Tarsus was a tentmaker, so his early work was the tent
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A doctrinal point is located in the apostle's first epistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early work of St Paul' suggests an epistle, but Acts says Paul made tents for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, a doctrine of a creed.

clue.text: Points to spy as source of papers

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four compass points
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Someone points a spy to where documents can be obtained.
explanation.definitionFit: The corner shop that sells daily newspapers and magazines is where you buy your paper.

clue.text: March past makes his day

parts.note: a march past sounds like a parade, but once the month of March is over the first of the next month is the prankster's day

explanation.surface: A military parade goes by and that makes one man's day.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of April, the day after March ends, belongs to a person duped by a hoax.

clue.text: Counters by reversing vehicle into capital

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or capital, written here with I for 1

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the word for it is read right to left

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up while backing a car into the city.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means 'first-class', and 'capital' is old British slang for excellent; the 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bead frames used for reckoning, tools on which one counts; the word is a plural of abacus.

clue.text: Street lights no longer provided for connecting roads

definitions.meaning: torches of pitch once carried by link-boys to light pedestrians through dark streets, now obsolete
roads joining one route to another, such as motorway slip roads

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both old flaming torches carried through streets and roads that join two others.

clue.text: Signify difficulty in obtaining entrance

parts.note: to spell is to mean or signify, as in 'this spells trouble'
a bind is a nuisance or difficult situation

explanation.surface: To indicate trouble getting in through the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a way in, but stressed on the second syllable it means to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold them in wonder, to cast a charm over them; obtaining that is the aim.

clue.text: Relaxed in good condition, of course

definitions.meaning: on a racecourse the going describes the state of the ground

explanation.definitionFit: It means placid and laid-back, and read as two words it describes comfortable ground underfoot on a course.

clue.text: Persevere with private cricket side

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
in cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: Keep going with a private member of the cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' is the army rank, not secret. In cricket the field divides into the leg or on side and the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going doggedly in the face of difficulty, like a soldier marching on.

clue.text: Fit worker to be a teller

parts.note: in form means fit and performing well
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A fit employee to become a bank teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teller' suggests a bank clerk, but here it is one who tells.
explanation.definitionFit: An informant tells things to others, giving information, often to the police.

clue.text: Bit food a little at a time

parts.note: a bit is a piece
a meal is food eaten at one sitting

explanation.surface: Someone nibbles at their dinner bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done gradually, in separate stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Star with heart of gold seen in capital after capital

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A star with a heart of gold appears in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after capital' pins the inserted letters right after the capital's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the North Star, is the bright star nearly over the north celestial pole.

clue.text: Breaks first order

indicators.note: to order something is to arrange it, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the first rule they were given.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifts are splits or cracks, openings where something has broken apart.

clue.text: Cover point, is he, at Headingley? Partly

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator asks whether a fielder at cover point is playing at Headingley.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a fielding position, but here it is a verb, to cover a point such as a blade. Headingley is a Test cricket ground in Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword is to put its point into a cover, the scabbard.

clue.text: Not an overall number, this sort

definitions.text: Not an overall number, this sort

parts.words: Not an overall number, this sort
parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, an anaesthetic; this kind deadens one area rather than the whole body

explanation.surface: Someone explains that this kind of figure is not a grand total.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs only part of the body, unlike a general one that puts the patient under.

clue.text: Thoroughly search end of the valley

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Search the far end of the valley thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of the valley' looks like one phrase, but 'end of' takes only the last letter of 'the', and 'valley' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short steep valley or hollow on a hillside, a word used in southern England.

clue.text: Strengthen Church control

annotationWithheld.why: 'Strengthen Church control' (9), printed so on the scan: REIN (control) + FORCE leaves Church unaccounted for, and REIN + FOR + CE needs a 'for' the clue lacks; no sound parse found

clue.text: Additional clause is carried

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a document or bill, an amendment
one who is carried along, as a passenger on a horse or bus

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an extra clause added to a legal document and someone borne along by a horse or vehicle.

clue.text: Dance for cast

definitions.meaning: the Highland ... is a lively Scottish dance
to cast is to throw or hurl

explanation.definitionFit: It names a vigorous Scottish dance and also means to throw something away forcefully.

clue.text: Knot tied, perhaps, around a number left over

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a knot tied in a handkerchief is a traditional memory aid, an example of a prompt to remember

explanation.surface: A knot is tied around a number of things that are still spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the knotted handkerchief as one example of a memory prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: In division, the remainder is what is left after the divisor goes in as many whole times as it can.

clue.text: Napoleon's invasion of Italy not opportune

indicators.note: an invasion of a country puts the invader inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: IT is the international vehicle code for Italy
nap is the short name of the card game Napoleon

explanation.surface: The French emperor's march into Italy was badly timed.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon looks like the emperor, but the card game called Napoleon is shortened to nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, the opposite of fitting the occasion.

clue.text: Inadequate type prepared to advance after a second

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a lender is someone willing to advance money

explanation.surface: A poor sort of person gets ready to move forward after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' reads as moving forward, but it means lending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means meagre or scant, as in slender means or a slender chance.

clue.text: Something worn in bed by American sleeper

parts.note: nigh means near, beside, so close by
in American usage a railway sleeper is called a tie

explanation.surface: Something worn in bed by a sleeping American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeper' suggests a person asleep, but it is the timber under rails, called a tie in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A short name for a nightdress, a garment worn to sleep in.
